title: candidate-feedback-draft-olivia-park-senior-backend-engineer
body:
Quick debrief / scratchpad for Olivia Park (applied: Senior Backend Engineer, serving runtime)

Context:
- Strong resume: previous infra work at mid-stage ML infra startup, shipped a custom request router and caching layer. Good systems background.
- Recruiting note: raised to onsites based on take-home and initial phone screen.

Interview loop summary (notes from interviewers):
- Rajesh (system design, scale): liked candidate's high-level approach to shuffle/sharding and KV cache invalidation; thought process on consistency vs availability was solid. Proposed practical mitigations (background compaction, versioned keys). Missed some low-level perf knobs (NUMA awareness, thread pinning) but recovered on follow-ups.
- Claire (runtime internals & observability): deep familiarity with profiling tools (perf, pprof). Proposed a good plan for diagnosing tokenization/latency regressions and an experiment plan to isolate KV cache miss patterns. Lacked familiarity with some of our internal tracing conventions but comfortable learning.
- Samir (storage + networking): good on network stack and RPC tradeoffs; suggested gRPC with multiplexing, eBPF-based metrics — overspecified in one area but pragmatic in tradeoffs discussion. Concern: limited exposure to CUDA/GPUs; candidate has little hands-on GPU runtime experience (mostly CPU-side infra).

Strengths:
- Clear thinker, explains tradeoffs well; pragmatic and delivery-oriented.
- Strong debugging and observability instincts.
- Good culture fit signals: collaborative, asks clarifying Qs, open to feedback.

Areas to probe further / risks:
- GPU/runtime inference experience: minimal. For serving-runtime role we rely on people who can at least read model runtime code and collaborate with low-level ML infra folks. Candidate can pair but may need ramp time.
- Low-level perf ops: understands profiling but less hands-on with kernel-level perf optimizations and GPU memory management.
- Ownership scope: uncertain whether they prefer platform-level long-lived ownership vs project-based feature work. Need to verify interest in long-term infra ownership.

Suggested follow-ups for final onsite:
- Systems design: focused exercise on a mixed CPU/GPU request router with latency SLOs (hard requirement: talk through KV cache warmup, fallback policies, and request routing if model variants exist).
- Practical task: read a small snippet of our runtime code (provide beforehand) and walk through where we'd add instrumentation + a concrete optimization plan.
- Behavioral: drive for ownership examples, long-lived systems ownership, on-call experience.

Score breakdown (rough):
- Systems design: 7/10
- Runtime internals / observability: 8/10
- Networking / storage: 7/10
- GPU/runtime familiarity: 4/10
- Culture / collaboration: 8/10

Recommendation (internal):
- Move to final onsite with clarified evaluation criteria around GPU/runtime familiarity. If team still feels uncertain after final loop, consider hiring for slightly more senior/experienced infra engineer or pairing this hire with a GPU-runtime-focused engineer.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Confirm candidate's willingness to own long-lived infra features (ask on loop).
- Share a small code snippet from our repo ahead of the onsite (Samir to prepare).
- Decide required minimum for GPU familiarity (ok if strong systems but light GPUs?) — align with hiring manager.

Notes-to-self: draft this as the official feedback doc after I collect any final comments by EOD 2026-03-06. If no objections, push to recruiting to schedule onsite.
